findings.problem: Double-undo is unguarded and the endpoint's own contract cannot be implemented. TASK-154's goal promises '409 if already reverted', but no reverted marker exists anywhere: TASK-044 only says 'consider marking a journal entry reverted after first successful undo', in an edge_cases bullet, and its steps 1-6 never add the field. A second undo re-runs RevertBookToVersion against a book_ver snapshot that the first undo already restored - TASK-044's own words: 'document this as a known no-op/idempotent-ish case but not guaranteed safe'. 'Not guaranteed safe' plus an HTTP endpoint that invites retries is a fail-open on the one path whose whole purpose is rollback.

findings.problem: TASK-107 adds a new rejection rule to ValidateOpDef, which is the server BOOT contract - a def it rejects makes the server refuse to start - and then explicitly authorises leaving non-compliant ops non-compliant: step 3 says to flag write-capable ops without dry_run support 'as a follow-up per-op task rather than silently forcing them'. Following the brief literally produces a binary that will not boot in prod, and the failure is at startup, i.e. after deploy, not in CI unless the boot smoke test happens to cover every plugin. There is no phased path (warn-then-enforce) and no rollback note.
findings.evidence: internal/operations/registry/registry.go:416-419 (HEAD): 'ValidateOpDef checks every rule an OperationDef must satisfy on its own... RegisterOp calls it first, so this function IS the boot contract: whatever it rejects here, the server refuses to start on.' Same file lines 420-428 record this exact failure mode having already happened twice ('the failure surfaced as the SERVER REFUSING TO BOOT -- twice'). Scale at HEAD: `grep -rln 'CapLibraryWrite' --include='*.go' internal/plugins | grep -v _test | wc -l` = 70 plugin files declare the write capability, while `grep -rln 'dry_run\|DryRun' --include='*.go' internal/plugins | grep -v _test | wc -l` = 17 mention a dry-run at all - so the audit step 3 waves through is on the order of 50 non-compliant defs, every one of which becomes a boot refusal.

TASK-107.steps_add: Two-phase rollout: PR 1 adds the field plus a WARN-only audit (log every write-capable def missing SupportsDryRun at boot) and sets the flag on every compliant op; PR 2 flips ValidateOpDef to reject, only once the audit logs zero. Never merge the rejecting rule while any registered def is non-compliant.

task_titles: Require every mutating operation to declare and enforce dry_run support at the registry

findings.problem: The task title says 'declare AND enforce dry_run support at the registry', but every step only implements DECLARE. After this lands, the registry gate reads as a guarantee ('registry enforces dry-run') while providing none - and step 4 concedes the param name is not even canonical ('some ops use apply inverted, some use dry_run'), so no runtime check is possible without first unifying the param.
findings.evidence: TASK-107 title: 'Require every mutating operation to declare and enforce dry_run support at the registry'. TASK-107.steps_add: Make the shared DryRunParams embed mandatory, not optional, and have the registry decode it centrally so the dispatcher (not the op body) is what refuses to write when dry_run is set. A declaration flag that nothing checks at runtime must not be described as enforcement.

findings.problem: Both tasks convert production APPLY ops from ResumeDrop to ResumeRestart. ResumeRestart is resumed automatically and unattended at server startup - no operator action, no gate. That directly collides with the standing rule that a running scan clobbers applied metadata and applies must never run during a scan (plan section 4 and DECISIONS row 14). After a deploy or crash-restart, an interrupted metadata.batch-apply-cached (which optionally writes tags to audio files on disk) or reconcile.apply (a dedup merge/apply path) will resume by itself, possibly into a scan window. Neither brief contains the words scan, interlock, or any precondition on resume.
findings.evidence: internal/operations/registry/resume.go:21-31 (HEAD): 'resumeAfterStartup is called from Start() before the dispatcher begins... ResumeRestart: increment resume_count, dispatch with saved state.' resume.go:117-129: '_ = r.store.UpdateOperationV2Status(row.ID, "queued", ...)' then 'r.pingDispatch()'. Master plan section 4 Wave 4: 'A running scan clobbers applied metadata - never apply during a scan. This constraint binds most of Wave 4.' DECISIONS-PENDING.md row 14: 'E02 never via library.scan while applies are pending'. grep of both briefs for 'scan' returns no hit in steps/edge_cases/acceptance.

TASK-147.steps_add: Before RunItems resumes, check for an active library.scan / reconcile_scan op and park (or refuse) rather than resume; add a test asserting a resumed apply does not start while a scan op is running.

findings.problem: resumeRestart is fail-OPEN when the checkpoint is missing, unreadable, or schema_version=1: it logs and dispatches the op with the ORIGINAL params, i.e. ResumeFrom absent => 0 => the entire book list is re-applied from the start. For metadata.batch-apply-cached with WriteBack=true that re-writes tags into audio files already processed; for reconcile.apply it re-applies every merge decision. Both briefs treat ResumeFrom=0 only as the benign 'fresh run' case and never as the checkpoint-lost case, so nothing in either task makes the resumed run safe when the state blob is gone.
findings.evidence: internal/operations/registry/resume.go:100-115: 'if stateRow, err := r.store.GetOpStateV2(row.ID); err == nil && stateRow != nil && stateRow.SchemaVersion == 2 { ... }' - every failure branch falls through with row.Params unchanged, then lines 117-129 re-queue and pingDispatch regardless. resume.go:88-91 doc comment: 'Schema_version=1 (gob) blobs are ignored - the op restarts from scratch once, which is safe for all idempotent ops.' TASK-147 EDGE_CASES: 'ResumeFrom=0 (a fresh run, not a resume) must behave identically to today's unconverted behavior - no skipped books.' - no checkpoint-lost case.

TASK-147.steps_add: Make the apply per-item idempotent (skip a book whose applied-revision already matches) OR refuse to resume when no schema_version=2 checkpoint is present, marking the op interrupted_ask instead. Add a test for 'checkpoint absent on restart' asserting no re-write.
TASK-147.edge_cases_add: Checkpoint row missing or schema_version=1 on resume: must NOT silently re-apply from index 0.

findings.problem: The owner decision that prod-data-path PRs are NOT auto-merged exists nowhere in the execution machinery. Every workstream's orchestration.md says 'Read the package-level ../../ORCHESTRATION.md first', and that document - docs/agent-tasks/ORCHESTRATION.md at HEAD - instructs the coordinator to open and rebase-merge every PR with no exception for review-critical work. The carve-out appears only as prose in BREAKDOWN and in each brief's header line, i.e. in documents the coordinator's git step does not consult. The default behaviour of the described machine is therefore to admin-merge 60 prod-data PRs unattended, overnight.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'PR left open\|stays open' docs/agent-tasks/todo-completion/*/orchestration.md` -> 0 hits across 18 files. Count: 60 of 189 tasks have review_critical=true.

findings.problem: Every brief's '## Idempotency / Rollback' section is boilerplate generated from the task's polarity field, and on data-touching tasks the claim it makes is FALSE. All 58 review-critical briefs carry one of exactly three sentences, each asserting that `git revert` restores the prior state: 'pre-existing behaviour is untouched (purely additive change)' (28), 'behaviour at the old site is restored' (27), 'no data or schema is touched' (3). The brief for the task that physically MOVES a survivor's audio files across the library says, verbatim, 'purely additive change'. Reverting the commit does not move files back, does not un-mint a backfilled sync identity, does not restore a compacted activity log, and does not re-write a config key the new binary stopped writing. The package therefore ships no real rollback story for exactly the 58 tasks that need one.
findings.evidence: `ls */TASK-*.md | wc -l` = 185 briefs; `grep -rlniE '## *rollback|rollback plan|how to revert' */TASK-*.md | wc -l` = 0 hand-written rollback plans. The selector is confirmed in the generator, not inferred: `sed -n '215,221p` of the package generator `scratchpad/gen_package.py` reads `pol = t.get("polarity") or "additive"` then `if pol == "additive": idem = ..."purely additive change").` / `elif pol == "removal": ..."no data or schema is touched".` / `else: ..."behaviour at the old site is restored".` - i.e. the rollback sentence is chosen by the polarity field alone, with no input from review_critical or from what the task writes. Extracting the section from the 58 briefs whose header carries '**REVIEW-CRITICAL' yields 3 distinct texts (28/27/3). dedup/TASK-052-physically-co-locate-a-combine-survivor-s-files-.md lines 104-106: '## Idempotency / Rollback\n\nIf the first acceptance check below already passes at HEAD ... Rollback = `git revert` the single commit; pre-existing behaviour is untouched (purely additive change).' - while its own Coordinator notes on the next line read 'review_critical because this touches CombineBooks, a prod-data merge/apply path with real file moves.' findings.problem: TASK-139 converts an option that currently cannot disable rate limiting into one that can, i.e. it makes a fail-open switch live - and it is marked review_critical=false, sonnet tier, with no step to check what production has persisted. The code's own warning text calls the disabled state 'vulnerable to abuse'. Because the flag's zero value is false, any persisted config row or env that carries a bare false (the exact 'stored zeros shadow defaults' class the package's own D111 note tracks) silently switches prod's API rate limiting OFF the moment this deploys, with only a WARN line as evidence.
findings.evidence: HEAD internal/server/server_lifecycle.go:1418-1419: 'if !config.AppConfig.EnableRateLimit { slog.Warn("rate limiting is disabled (enable_rate_limitfalse) - the API is vulnerable to abuse...") }' - the warning exists but the limiter is still built, because the build condition only tests rpm>0. Defaults are safe in code (internal/config/config.go:1292 'viper.SetDefault("enable_rate_limit", true)', :2337 'EnableRateLimit: true') but the field is a plain bool at :815 read via viper.GetBool at :1706, so a persisted false wins. findings.problem: TASK-169 fans DismissDedupCluster's per-candidate work out over runtime.NumCPU() goroutines, and the per-candidate work calls EmbeddingStore.UpsertLabeledExample - one of the few EmbeddingStore methods that does NOT take the store's closeMu read lock, only a check-then-act atomic flag. The file's own comment documents that this exact shape deadlocked three concurrent writers inside db.Set for 29 minutes in CI. The brief's only mitigation is 'grep for other concurrent callers of these methods elsewhere as a precedent check' - a precedent grep is not a concurrency proof, and the repo's concurrency rule explicitly says to check for shared mutable state rather than assume.
findings.evidence: internal/database/dedup_label.go:111-120: 'func (s *EmbeddingStore) UpsertLabeledExample(ex LabeledExample) error { if err := s.checkClosed(); err != nil {...} ... return s.db.Set(dedupLabelKey(ex.CandidateID), data, pebble.Sync) }' - no closeMu. internal/database/embedding_store.go:269-274 shows checkClosed is only 's.closed.Load()'. Contrast embedding_store.go:331,341,403,429,453,563,757 which all do 's.closeMu.RLock(); defer s.closeMu.RUnlock()'. embedding_store.go:209-218: 'closeMu serialises every DB-touching operation against Close ... doing so deadlocks for real: three writers inside db.Set blocked forever on commitPipeline.prepare and hung TestChaos_MixedReadWriteDuringClose for 29 minutes (CI run 31603570061). The pre-existing closed flag below cannot prevent that - it is a check-then-act'. TASK-169 STEPS: 'Verify h ... and es ... are safe for concurrent calls ... grep for other concurrent callers of these methods elsewhere in the codebase as a precedent check.'
